anthropic.why: Messages requires max_tokens; 8192 is the conservative default when no cap is configured
notes: Chat and Responses omit an unconfigured output cap and let the endpoint choose its default.

model_id_forms.why: A gateway id in canonical vendor/model form is matched by its model part only for these canonical vendor slugs
notes: A different vendor prefix keeps the id unknown even when its suffix would match a rule; a custom alias such as production-model stays unknown and is probed.

off.description: Do not add provider-specific reasoning fields.

responses.effort.description: Put the resolved effort in a Responses reasoning object when one exists.

reasoning.object.description: Use a nested reasoning object on normalized OpenAI-compatible gateways.

reasoning.effort.description: Use the OpenAI-compatible reasoning_effort field, including an explicit off spelling.

thinking.with-effort.description: Toggle thinking.type and send the resolved effort beside it.

thinking.toggle.description: Toggle thinking.type without an effort field.

thinking.effort.description: Toggle thinking.type and use reasoning_effort for the thinking depth.

enable-thinking.description: Toggle the enable_thinking boolean used by compatible gateways.

mandatory.description: The model always reasons and needs no request-side toggle.

messages.manual.description: Enable Anthropic manual thinking with a bounded token budget.

messages.manual-opus-45.description: Combine Opus 4.5 manual thinking with its limited output effort control.

messages.adaptive.description: Use Anthropic adaptive thinking and the model's resolved output effort.

messages.adaptive-xhigh-as-max.description: Use adaptive thinking on models that accept max but not xhigh.

model_rules.why: GPT-6 always reasons from low to max, with no none effort
notes: GPT-6 drops none and minimal; low is the floor and thinking cannot be disabled.

model_rules.why: minimal is not a spelling on gpt-5.6
the Pro models reject anything below medium, and have no max
the Codex models have neither minimal nor max
this generation dropped minimal, and max is not a spelling here
gpt-5.1 predates xhigh and max, and has no minimal
gpt-5-pro runs at high and takes no other level
gpt-5 predates xhigh and max
the o-series predates minimal, xhigh and max
DeepSeek V4 Pro serves a low request as high
DeepSeek serves medium and xhigh as high
K3 has no medium or xhigh, and cannot stop thinking
Kimi K2.5 and K2.6 expose hybrid thinking through thinking.type
Kimi K2.7 Code is thinking-only and preserves reasoning across turns
Kimi Code's K3 has no medium or xhigh
notes: reasoning_effort none disables thinking and routes away from K3; it remains an explicit off override rather than a K3 effort level.

model_rules.why: Kimi For Coding uses the thinking-only K2.7 Code contract
GLM-5.3 has no medium or xhigh, and cannot stop thinking
GLM-5.2 serves anything but high as max

Grok 4.6 adds xhigh and cannot stop reasoning
Grok 4.5 serves an xhigh request as high, and cannot stop reasoning
3.1 Pro maps minimal to low, rejects xhigh, and cannot stop reasoning
Gemini Flash rejects xhigh and max, and always thinks
2.5 gives minimal and low the same budget; Pro cannot stop reasoning
2.5 gives minimal and low the same 1,024-token budget, and disables with none
Qwen3.8-Max has no minimal, and neither high nor max is a spelling

model_rules.why: These families always reason; off is not a choice
notes: Always-thinking families keep thinking active even when a config names off: the adaptive recipe's disable step is gated on reasoning.mandatory.

model_rules.why: Opus 4.5 uniquely combines manual thinking with output_config.effort
4.5 and earlier require manual thinking
notes: Unknown aliases receive no generation recipe; guessing can turn a valid alias into HTTP 400.
History: Sonnet/Haiku 4.5 and earlier keep only the latest turn's thinking; Opus 4.5 keeps all (matched above).

model_rules.why: This generation uses adaptive thinking and maps xhigh to max
notes: 4.6 rejects manual thinking and has no xhigh spelling yet; xhigh requests are served as max.

model_rules.why: 4.7+ adaptive thinking takes the full effort scale
notes: 4.7+ rejects manual thinking; only adaptive is offered.

model_rules.why: OpenAI documents gpt-5.x and gpt-6 tool calling on the Responses API
OpenAI reasoning controls apply only to documented reasoning model families

providers.why: Chat reasoning controls, strict schemas, temperature suppression, and Responses server tools apply only where OpenAI documents them
notes: The Responses reasoning object is limited to reasoning families; GPT-4.1 supports Responses but is non-reasoning.
Only web_search is admitted as a server tool; other hosted tools require resource or approval lifecycles not implemented here.

providers.why: OpenRouter normalizes upstream reasoning and server tools behind its own request shapes
notes: reasoning and history model traits are ignored because sending an upstream model's native spelling would bypass OpenRouter's normalized contract.

model_rules.why: OpenCode Zen routes Claude and Qwen model IDs through Messages
OpenCode Zen routes GPT and Grok model IDs through Responses

providers.why: One OpenCode base URL multiplexes wire protocols by model, so api=auto cannot infer the protocol from the URL
notes: Zen documents its websearch and webfetch features as client tools, not API server tools; builtin_tools_by_wire therefore remains empty.

providers.why: DeepSeek uses thinking.type plus its own effort scale, omits OpenAI prompt_cache_key, and requires beta routing for strict function schemas
notes: Ordinary turns may omit prior reasoning, but assistant tool-call messages must retain it.
DeepSeek's Chat schema accepts function tools only, so no provider-side tools are admitted.

model_rules.why: GLM-5.3 keeps its own scale on Alibaba
Alibaba serves low and medium as high for these models

providers.why: Qwen's endpoint owns history preservation and re-hosted effort scales, while Responses exposes a limited server-tool set
notes: web_search and web_extractor are Responses server tools; Chat search is configured in the request body instead.

providers.why: The international and China Kimi API domains expose the same model controls, fixed temperature behavior, and builtin web search contract
notes: The $web_search builtin function is a Chat tool entry that the model calls back; it is not a client-side search shortcut.

providers.why: Kimi Code is a separate subscription API whose official WebSearch and FetchURL tools run on the client
notes: No coding-endpoint server-tool contract is assumed.

providers.why: Z.AI domains share thinking controls, automatic context caching, and a Chat web_search tool shape
notes: Retrieval and server MCP are not admitted because their result lifecycles are not implemented.

providers.why: China's BigModel endpoint documents the same thinking, automatic-cache, and Chat web_search contracts

model_rules.why: Volcengine Ark gives every model it hosts these four levels

providers.why: Ark applies one endpoint-owned effort scale to every hosted model, overriding upstream model scales
notes: DeepSeek and GLM therefore use Ark's four levels here rather than their upstream scales.

providers.why: Anthropic web search is a versioned Messages server-tool definition
notes: Only the tested web_search_20250305 definition is admitted.
